## p204 A — Local radio station to be handed over to Poland

**Edition context:** p204 A — a radio-station handover and a conditional date digit.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-p204-a-p204-a--a-radio-station-handover-and-a-conditional-date-digit"></a>



**Status:** The unchanged published `Nov16-18` partial key fixes **69 of 70
plaintext positions** from all **140 valid source coordinates**. The only
unknown is a date digit. A separately recorded calendar inference gives a
plausible new assignment, **FD = 8**, without changing the published key.
**Source review and inference:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro. The period key
retains the attribution in [data/keys.json](../data/keys.json).

<a id="edition-cases-radio-p204-a-reading-from-the-published-key"></a>

### Reading from the published key

**Readable German:**

> Hiesige Fusta wird laut S.R. Warschau Montag 1? Polen uebergeben.
> Fusta WAUM.

**Meaning:** According to S.R. Warsaw, the local radio station is to be handed
over to Polish control on Monday the 1?. `Fusta` is read as the abbreviated
radio station. `S.R.` is likely the Soldiers' Council in this context, but its
expansion is not part of the decrypted character stream. The raw ending
`FUSTAWAUM` is retained; its final `M` is not silently changed to a separator
or a different call sign.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
HIESIGEFUSTAWIRDLAUTXSXRXWARSCHAUMONTAGX1?XPOLENUEBERGEBENXXFUSTAWAUMX
```

</details>

Every fixed letter above comes from valid source coordinates and an already
established square cell. No editorial coordinate repair is proposed for this
message.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-p204-a-source-date"></a>

### Source date

The [source image](../experiments/open_targets_continuation/sources/childs_p204_selected.png)
is printed p204 / PDF page 207, section A. The heading reads **16 November 1918**;
the intercept and internal stamps are:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
LP v WAU (3.20 a.m., November 17th)
SN AR KRIEGSMINISTERIUM 2130 (16)
RICHI-140
```

</details>

The body preserves every one of the 140 printed coordinates. The date's
unknown unit at plaintext index **41** uses the fully observed digraph
**FD**, square cell **13** in zero-based row-major indexing. Its source
coordinates are indices **92** and **63**. Under the published partial square,
its domain is `03456789`.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-p204-a-why-18-november-is-a-strong-conditional-reading"></a>

### Calendar evidence for the conditional 18 November reading

The preceding digit `1` and the word `MONTAG` are directly fixed. If the
date refers to **November 1918**, as the message heading and internal stamp
indicate, the compatible candidates are:

| Day in November 1918 | Weekday |
| ---: | --- |
| 10 | Sunday |
| 13 | Wednesday |
| 14 | Thursday |
| 15 | Friday |
| 16 | Saturday |
| 17 | Sunday |
| **18** | **Monday** |
| 19 | Tuesday |

The 11th was also a Monday, but the unknown cell cannot contain `1`: that
digit already occupies another established cell in the injective square.
The 12th is likewise excluded because `2` is already assigned. Thus
**Monday 18 November** is the unique candidate under the stated month,
weekday and square assumptions.

This is a historical inference, not an extra character supplied by the
unchanged key. It assumes that the weekday, month context and two date
coordinates were copied correctly. Source copying errors remain possible.
The repository therefore keeps `FD = 8` in the
[conditional layer](../experiments/open_targets_continuation/certificates.json),
leaving the published partial square untouched.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-p204-a-independent-consequences"></a>

### Independent consequences

The same `FD` cell appears in three date fields of the three-part
[p206 A reference list](201.md#edition-cases-military-p201-p206-orders). Under the conditional assignment,
all three read **8 November**. This is propagation of one shared key cell,
not three independent confirmations of its value.

None of the six unresolved reference digits in the
[p205 financial](205.md#edition-cases-finance-p205-a) and [naval](205.md#edition-cases-naval-p205-b) messages uses `FD`.
Consequently, this inference alone supplies **no new fixed p205 character**;
it only removes `8` from the domains of their other unassigned cells.
The separate p201/p206 date-link inference supplies one p205 digit under a
different, explicitly recorded assumption.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-p204-a-verification-and-credit"></a>

### Verification and credit

```sh
python3 experiments/open_targets_continuation/verify.py --verify
```

The verifier independently reconstructs the column offsets, checks the
plaintext domains against the project decoder, reproduces the calendar
calculation and lists every position affected by the conditional assignment.
The [inputs](../experiments/open_targets_continuation/inputs.json) preserve
the literal source, exact header, source-image hash and assumptions.
The source review and conditional analysis are by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**;
no first-decipherment priority is claimed for this supplementary message.

## Armistice acknowledgments, personnel and Warsaw radio inquiries

**Sources on this page:** p204 B, p204 C1, p204 D.

**Related source pages:** [p202 A1](202.md#source-p202-a1), [p202 A2](202.md#source-p202-a2), [p203 A2](203.md#source-p203-a2), [p203 B](203.md#source-p203-b).

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov16-18-command-inquiries-armistice-acknowledgments-personnel-and-warsaw-radio-inquiries"></a>



**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Seven native source records cover an armistice-receipt query, nightly radio listening, an inquiry for Captain von Borries, the location of the Warsaw general government, and radio equipment and personnel. Two previously OCR-damaged short messages become clear when their actually printed final groups are restored. All unresolved fields and missing-letter spellings remain explicit.

### p204 C1

**Source transcription — header:** `C) KOW v WAU (1.50 a.m., November 18th); 0115 (17), 2 TLE; 1 TL RICHI-244`

**Readable German — repaired output:**

> GE?NACH2O2. Leichte in Lomza und Czenstochau, Verbleib unbekannt. Vermutl. mit ihren Gouvs. aberueckt. Besatzg beiden anderen Stat. ohne Geraet.

**Meaning:** The whereabouts of the light units or equipment in Lomza and Czenstochau are unknown; they are presumed to have departed with their governors. The crews of the other two stations have no equipment. The opening is opaque and several transmitted abbreviations and the missing-letter spelling ABERUECKT remain visible.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output** — every native source slot in printed order, under the stated published key.

```text
GE?NACH2O2LE?CHTEINLOMZAUNDCZENSTOCHAUXV?RBLEIBUNBEKANNTXVERMUTLMITI?RENGOUVSABERUECKTXBESATZGBEIDENANDERE?STATOHNEGERA?TX
```

**Edited output** — 2 observed-coordinate substitutions and 3 source-mask fills; no coordinate inserted, deleted or moved.

```text
GE?NACH2O2LEICHTEINLOMZAUNDCZENSTOCHAUXVERBLEIBUNBEKANNTXVERMUTLMITIHRENGOUVSABERUECKTXBESATZGBEIDENANDERENSTATOHNEGERAETX
```

**Unresolved details and editorial limits:**

- The source prints four dash slots: XD--- and GG-AX. The opening GE?NACH2O2 remains unresolved.

- Part 2 advertises 282 slots but the reviewed page prints 242. A 40-slot tail-loss hypothesis yields related fragments, but is not accepted as a complete source-length decipherment or counted as another reviewed reading here.

### Evidence and credit

Published period keys: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier unreviewed repository candidates are preserved separately. This is a source edition and explicit repair review, not a claim of universal first-decipherment priority.

The certificates replay every coordinate alteration, compare the independent column/domain reconstruction with the cipher implementation, and re-encrypt every complete edited output. For partial outputs, each certificate also constructs one injective global completion of the square and residual masks and verifies its full round-trip; the witness is explicitly nonhistorical. Each readable passage preserves every nonseparator output label; literal protected fields are also checked without removing their internal separators. Source crops are bound to the original PDF by page, rectangle, scale, file digest and RGB-pixel digest.

Reproduce with `python experiments/nov16_18_command_inquiries/verify.py --verify`. Add `--pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf` to regenerate and compare the delivered source pixels.

A round-trip proves compatibility with a stated reading. Editorial spelling repairs remain proposals, and literal number labels are not automatically historical dates, quantities or reference numbers.

## p204 C2 — Conditional lost-row reading: radio handover and WAU personnel transfer

**Edition context:** Warsaw station report: a conditional missing-row continuation.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-warsaw-station-missing-row-warsaw-station-report-a-conditional-missing-row-continuation"></a>



**Source review and conditional reconstruction: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Childs p204 C2 prints **242 coordinate slots** but advertises **282**. Inserting a hypothetical row of eight five-coordinate groups before the terminal `GX` produces a coherent continuation of [part 1](#edition-cases-radio-nov16-18-command-inquiries-p204-c1): equipment has not arrived from home, operation is to pass to the Poles on Monday evening, and WAU is transferring personnel. The proposed words require **no change to any observed coordinate** and **36 fills in the 40 hypothesized missing slots**. Four plaintext positions remain unknown.

The longer frame and those 36 fills remain a **conditional reconstruction**. The scan does not visibly mark a lost row, and no complete independent copy supplies it. The native 242-slot decoding remains available below.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-warsaw-station-missing-row-p204-c2"></a>

### p204 C2

[Reviewed source excerpt](../experiments/warsaw_station_missing_row/sources/p204_C.png) · [Exact inputs](../experiments/warsaw_station_missing_row/inputs.json) · [All gap placements and global witnesses](../experiments/warsaw_station_missing_row/certificates.json)

**Source transcription — header:** `C) KOW v WAU (1.50 a.m., November 18th); 0115 (17), 2 TLE; 2 TL RICHI-282`.

The seven printed lines contain six lines of 40 coordinates and a final two-coordinate group `GX`. This count restores several groups omitted or damaged by OCR, but the remaining 40-slot discrepancy is in the reviewed source itself.

**Readable German — conditional interpretation**, from the edited 282-slot frame with the missing row inserted before `GX`:

> Das nicht aus Heimat eingetroffen. NO?A WAU. Festfern, Festfunk A uebergeben Betrieb Montag Abend Polen. S. R. WAU ueberweist Mannschaften Bezkdos des ?K? nach OA?.

**Meaning:** The preceding part ends with equipment; this continuation says it has not arrived from home. Under the stated lost-row hypothesis, the facilities designated FESTFERN and FESTFUNK A hand operation to the Poles on Monday evening, and S. R. WAU transfers personnel to the abbreviated Bezkdos. The opening token, final unit and destination are not identified.

The literal tokens `NO?A`, `A` after `FESTFUNK`, `DES?K?` and `OA?` are retained. `Bezkdos` is left as the transmitted abbreviation. The ending is not silently made into a fluent unit name or a plausible destination.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-warsaw-station-missing-row-what-the-terminal-alternatives-establish"></a>

### Terminal gap alternatives under the proposed wording

The verifier checks every possible start for one contiguous 40-slot gap against the same disclosed word template. Exactly three terminal placements allow the proposed wording without changing an observed coordinate. This is a compatibility result **conditioned on the proposed wording**, not an independent identification of the lost position.

| Missing gap starts at source index | Position relative to terminal GX | Inserted-slot fills | Fixed edited positions | Remaining ending |
| ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 240 | Before GX | 36 | 137 / 141 | `DES?K?NACHOA?X` |
| 241 | Between G and X | 35 | 136 / 141 | `?ES?K?NACHOA?X` |
| 242 | After GX | 34 | 135 / 141 | `?ES?K?NACH?A?X` |

The before-`GX` placement preserves the printed five-coordinate group boundary. The other two possibilities are retained because the observed coordinates and the selected words do not exclude them. All three branches preserve the same substantive middle reading while leaving different terminal fields open. No global key cell is reassigned.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-warsaw-station-missing-row-source-and-contextual-limits"></a>

### Source and contextual limits

The [preceding source part](#edition-cases-radio-nov16-18-command-inquiries-p204-c1) ends with crews of two other stations lacking equipment; `DAS NICHT AUS HEIMAT EINGETROFFEN` continues that sentence naturally. The independently reviewed [p204 A telegram](#edition-cases-radio-p204-a) also reports a Monday handover to the Poles. These are useful contextual checks, but neither provides this part's missing ciphertext, final reference or destination.
